points.heading: What we learned
points.body:
This week you learned three Spanish verb families: **-ar**, **-er**, and **-ir** in the present.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Let's practice point 1
points.body:
**-ar** with **cantar**: yo **canto**, tú **cantas**, él **canta** — drop -ar, then add the ending.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Let's practice point 2
points.body:
**-er** with **comer**: yo **como**, tú **comes**, él **come** — hear the -es/-e endings.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Let's practice point 3
points.body:
**-ir** with **vivir**: yo **vivo**, tú **vives**, él **vive** — same person pattern as -er here.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

points.heading: Synthesis
points.body:
If you can fill a yo/tú/él chart for all three families, you hold the heart of the week.

Practice: Your turn. Say the key idea out loud.

Common mistake: Mixing up two different points.

lesson.summary: In this lesson, you will use Spanish verb endings to say who does an action.
lesson.memoryPhrase: Spanish families: **-ar** (cantar → canto, cantas, canta), **-er** (comer → como, comes, come), **-ir** (vivir → vivo, vives, vive).
